name: platform-tls-verify-policy
title: Reverse HTTPS exact-target TLS verification policy
description: Define operator-authorized exact-target VERIFY, custom CA, and BYPASS behavior with direct/routed parity, revocation, and failure attribution without expanding Resin into a CA/PKI lifecycle manager.
creator: killbus
notes: The design target is fixed: a request authorized by the shared admin token configures exact HTTPS host:port rules selecting custom CA trust or explicit BYPASS; absent rules use VERIFY and no VERIFY row is persisted. CABundleRegistry centrally imports, canonicalizes, fingerprints, deduplicates, verifies, and delete-restricts immutable CA bundles; PlatformTLSPolicy separately owns platform exact-target rules and fixed bundle-ID binding. Every active-rule mutation uses expected-absence/current-version CAS with history in the same transaction. Import has no authorization effect, and neither module performs the other's mutations. TRUST_CUSTOM_CA is target-exclusive: it uses only the bound bundle while retaining hostname/SNI, validity, and chain verification, with no system-root augmentation or fallback. Persisted policies are an exhaustive discriminated union: TRUST_CUSTOM_CA requires only bundle_id, while BYPASS requires only reason/expiry; mode switches replace a complete variant and database constraints reject cross-mode fields. Active executable rules, PEM-free rule history, and PEM-free bundle lifecycle events are separate; platform/rule deletion records terminal history before removing active state and never cascade-deletes history. Resin has no user/RBAC or distinct administrator identity. The first version persists canonical CA PEM and versioned fingerprint in Resin strong state without external secret references; full PEM stays out of list responses, ordinary logs, and audit event bodies. BYPASS create requires explicit expires_at: null means permanent and future RFC3339 means temporary; PATCH omission is unchanged and explicit null sets permanent. At expiry, temporary BYPASS resolves to strict VERIFY for new requests and cannot reuse idle BYPASS connections. BYPASS also requires a trimmed non-empty reason on create/mode-switch and a new reason when extending the expiry or making it permanent; the reason is versioned audit context, not actor identity or proof of approval. The same decision applies to direct and routed reverse requests under the shared proxy token. Broader matchers, automatic downgrade, identity expansion, CA private keys, issuance, and PKI lifecycle are out of scope. History retention/purge behavior and the evidence threshold for node health attribution remain open implementation contracts; handshake-scoped revocation is closed: new requests cut over at snapshot publication, idle profiles close, and existing in-flight/streaming/upgrade sessions drain naturally.
